attributes.action: Review and reform Plan 2 student loan repayment terms
attributes.additional_details: Many Plan 2 graduates repay their loans for decades while their balances continue to grow due to high interest rates and frozen repayment thresholds. This disproportionately affects middle earners, reduces take-home pay during a cost of living crisis, and makes the system feel unfair and unclear. A review would help ensure the system remains sustainable and aligned with its original intent.
attributes.background: Review Plan 2 student loan repayment thresholds and interest rates, including the impact of frozen thresholds. Assess whether current terms are fair, transparent, and proportionate, and consider reforms so repayments reduce balances and better reflect graduates’ ability to pay.

other_parliamentary_business.body:
The Government has responded to a public (paper) petition calling for student loan repayment threshold freezes to be reversed and student loan interest rates to be reviewed to restore fairness. The petition was presented to the House of Commons by Tom Gordon MP on behalf of residents of the United Kingdom.

* Read the petition and the Government's response[1]

The petition asks the House of Commons to request the Government backtrack on freezing student loan repayment thresholds and review student loan interest rates to restore fairness.

In response to the petition's request, the Government states that they are reforming higher education funding and regulation to better support disadvantaged students, make things fairer for graduates, and create a more flexible post-16 education system. Key measures include increasing maintenance loans in line with forecast inflation, making care leavers automatically eligible for the maximum rate of maintenance loan from 2026 to 2027, and re-introducing targeted, means-tested maintenance grants from 2028 to 2029. For graduates, maximum interest rates on plan 2 and 3 student loans will be capped at 6% from 1 September 2026, while the plan 2 repayment threshold has increased to £29,385 and will remain at that level until April 2030. The student finance system continues to remove up-front financial barriers to higher education, provides protections for lower-earning graduates, and remains heavily subsidised by Government, with a significant proportion of loans expected to be written off as a deliberate investment in people and the economy.

What are public (paper) petitions?

A public (paper) petition is a petition to the House of Commons presented by an MP.

* Find out more about public (paper) petitions[2]

Get involved in the work of the UK Parliament

You can also sign up[3] to the UK Parliament newsletter for the latest information on how to get involved and make a difference.
